free_tier.stated: 10 GB of encrypted backup storage free, with no credit card and no expiry: 2 devices and 7 days of snapshot history, over a private Restic REST endpoint on a per-customer ZFS dataset. Paid vaults: Starter USD 3 a month for 250 GB, 10 devices and 30-day history; Standard USD 9 a month for 1 TB, 25 devices and 60-day history; Pro USD 17 a month for 2 TB, 50 devices and 90-day history; Business USD 45 a month for 5 TB, 100 devices and 180-day history; a Lite vault of 100 GB at USD 2 a month; vaults from 6 TB at USD 8 per TB a month. The Business tier is a dated observation: the page read on 2026-10-22 marked it 'Opening soon, join the waitlist', and the page read on 2026-10-30 marks it 'Available on request: contact us'. The same host sells KVM cloud servers on NVMe from USD 3 a month, Proxmox Backup Server datastores, hosted Borg repositories and website hosting, and states no egress fees on restore. Annual billing is ten months for twelve.

per_object_cap.notes: no per-object cap is published; the plan caps the vault's total stored bytes

retention.stated: The free tier has no expiry ('10 GB free tier never expires'). Snapshot history is kept 7 days on Free, 30 on Starter, 60 on Standard, 90 on Pro and 180 on Business; on cancellation the page states 'Cancel anytime, snapshots stay.'
retention.notes: snapshot history is a per-plan window; the account itself has no stated expiry

egress.terms: no egress fees on restore, and no restore penalties or per-API-call charges stated; the vendor also states no egress fees on the cloud server line
egress.free_allowance: unmetered egress; the free tier is capped at 10 GB of stored bytes

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: plain Restic over HTTPS against a private REST endpoint. On Linux one command copied from the portal installs Restic, creates the encryption key, runs the first backup and schedules the next; on macOS and Windows standard restic is pointed at the vault URL and token. status.servercrate.net publishes a restore-verification check. It is a backup target and not a filesystem, so it is not mounted like a bucket
chaining: 10 GB free with client-side encryption, no egress fee and no expiry is an offsite copy for small state: configuration, keys and indexes. It does not hold bulk data: past 10 GB the paid vaults run to 5 TB at USD 45 a month, and USD 8 per TB a month from 6 TB.

limits.value: the binding count is stored bytes rather than transferred bytes: 10 GB on the free tier against a stated 'no backup or bandwidth caps' and 'No egress fees on restore'. The seven vocabulary kinds have no separate name for a storage-size cap, so this is filed as volume-quota and the distinction is stated here rather than left to the kind. Nothing binds on transfer.

identity_cost.detail: The free signup form asks for an email address and a password of at least 12 characters, with full name optional, behind a Cloudflare Turnstile check and a proof-of-work field; its subtitle reads 'Free encrypted vault - no credit card needed'. No card, phone or ID field is on the form. Paid plans are paid by card through Stripe, PayPal or on-chain Bitcoin.

reliability_note: The status page read on 2026-10-30 shows every monitored component operational and no active incident. The incidents page read on 2026-10-30 lists 2 incidents in 2026, each resolved the same day with no stored data lost: on 2026-09-27 vault creation failed for some new signups; on 2026-08-09 a rate limit shared by every vault returned temporary HTTP 503 responses to backup requests under load, seen only on the vendor's internal test vaults with no customer backup failed, and the limits are now per vault at 16 connections and 60 requests per second.
